definition.name: NXlaser_pump_probe

symbol.name: nE
symbol.doc: Number of recorded events. An event is one pump pulse and the probe measurement that belongs to it: a laser shot at a high-power laser, one pump-probe pair at a beamline, one pulse in a pulse train at a free-electron laser. Every per-event array in the entry has this length and the order of ``/ENTRY/events/identifier``.

symbol.name: nC
symbol.doc: Number of points in a temporal-contrast trace.

definition.doc:
Laser pump, any probe: the part of a pump-probe experiment that laser facilities, synchrotron beamlines with a laser and free-electron lasers have in common.
A laser pulse (the pump) excites a sample, and a probe pulse (X-rays, light, electrons or ions) measures it a set time later. This definition records the two beams, the delay between them, what that delay is held against, and the identity of each event. It does not describe the probe measurement itself (diffraction, reflectivity, spectroscopy, imaging): that belongs to the technique's own application definition in the same entry, or to the facility's detector groups.
**Core and modules.** Only the core is required. Everything else is optional and belongs to one module, named at the start of its description, so that each facility uses the modules that fit its experiments:
* MODULE high-intensity: relativistic and laser-plasma experiments (temporal contrast, focal spot, peak intensity, a0, amplification state, laser-driven secondary sources, destroyed targets). * MODULE accelerator-probe: probes from a storage ring or free-electron laser (bunch pattern, RF locking, arrival-time correction, pulses inside trains, gated detectors). * MODULE high-repetition: kHz to MHz pumping (pump-on/pump-off events, pulse picking, readbacks on their own clock). * MODULE surfaces: grazing incidence on surfaces and interfaces (fluence per footprint, incidence geometry, samples with persistent identifiers). * MODULE long-pulse: nanosecond and shaped pulses, for example shock compression (the temporal pulse shape). * MODULE simulation: links to particle-in-cell or other simulations. * MODULE provenance: the diagnostic and laser-chain metadata of the HELPMI Devices, Detectors and Components library (technical, procedural and access metadata), as in the PHELIX and POLARIS example files.
A facility that needs some of these always, or needs more, writes a short definition that extends this one and makes those items required (see the site definitions next to this file). Anyone else uses this definition as it is.
**Layouts.** Both common layouts are valid: one entry per campaign with per-event arrays of length nE, or one entry per event with nE = 1.
**Conventions.**
* The pump defines time zero. ``pulse_delay`` is stored on the probe beam with ``@reference_beam`` pointing to the pump beam, and is positive when the probe reaches the interaction point after the pump. * Fields hold readback values; target values use the reserved ``_set`` suffix and uncertainties the ``_errors`` suffix. * A value that held for the whole entry is a scalar. A value that changed from event to event is an array of length nE, in the order of ``/ENTRY/events/identifier``. Values sampled on their own clock go in ``NXlog`` groups. * Beam quantities are given at the interaction point unless the beam group's ``distance`` or ``depends_on`` says otherwise.

field.name: definition
field.doc: Official NeXus NXDL schema to which this subentry conforms.

field.name: start_time
field.doc: Start of the first event. ISO 8601 with an explicit time zone.

field.name: experiment_identifier
field.doc: The campaign, beamtime or proposal this entry belongs to, as the facility names it.

group.name: events
group.doc:
The event list. Its ``identifier`` is the axis every per-event array in the entry refers to. Per-event readbacks (pump energy, delay, lock state) are linked here as auxiliary signals, not copied.
PROPOSED: NeXus has per-pulse identifiers only for neutron event data and atom-probe pulses. This group gives a pump-probe event one identity, issued once, at the source.

field.name: identifier
field.doc: The identity of each event as its issuer assigned it: the shot number from a shot authority, a pulse-train identifier, a bunch or frame number. A number or a string, unique within the issuer.

attribute.name: issuer
attribute.doc: Who assigned the identifier, for example "HZDR DRACO shot authority" or "European XFEL timing system (train ID)". Identifiers from different issuers are never compared.

field.name: time
field.doc: When each event happened, as the issuer recorded it. ISO 8601 with an explicit time zone.

field.name: status
field.doc: What kind of event it was. An analysis normally keeps only ``shot``. The values are LabFrog's shot statuses.

field.name: sub_index
field.doc: MODULE accelerator-probe. Position of the event inside the issuer's unit, when one identifier covers several events, for example the pulse index inside a pulse train.

field.name: pump_state
field.doc: MODULE high-repetition. Whether the pump reached the sample in this event. Unpumped events are the reference that pumped events are compared with. (Not "on"/"off": YAML reads those as booleans.)

field.name: amplification_state
field.doc: MODULE high-intensity. PROPOSED. How far the pump laser was amplified for this event. Alignment and diagnostic shots at reduced energy are common, and the HELPMI library asks for laser data to be kept "even if not fully-amplified".

group.name: source_pump
group.doc: The laser that generates the pump beam.

field.name: frequency
field.doc: Repetition rate of the pump at the sample, after any pulse picking. Single-shot lasers give the shot rate they ran at.

field.name: associated_beam
field.doc: Path to the pump beam, ``/ENTRY/INSTRUMENT/beam_pump``. FROM NXmpes: this field is not in the NXsource base class; the NXmpes application definition introduced it, and this definition reuses it unchanged. Moving it (and ``associated_source``) into the base classes would let any definition pair a source with its beam.

group.name: pulse_shape
group.doc: MODULE long-pulse. The temporal shape of the delivered pulse (``NXsource/pulse_shape``), for shaped nanosecond pulses.
Manufacturer and model of the laser.

group.name: source_probe
group.doc: The source of the probe: a storage ring, a free-electron laser, the same laser (an optical probe split from the pump), or a laser-driven secondary source.

field.name: type
field.doc: PROPOSED enumeration items for laser-driven secondary sources (the list is open, so they are valid now): "Laser Plasma X-ray Source", "Laser Plasma Ion Source", "Laser Plasma Electron Source".

field.name: associated_beam
field.doc: Path to the probe beam, ``/ENTRY/INSTRUMENT/beam_probe``. FROM NXmpes, as for ``source_pump``.

field.name: previous_source
field.doc: MODULE high-intensity. For a secondary source driven by a laser, the path to that laser's NXsource; for an optical probe split from the pump laser, the path to ``source_pump``. A chain of sources (a laser driving a mediator target that emits the probe) is a chain of ``previous_source`` links.

field.name: mode
field.doc: MODULE accelerator-probe. Storage-ring operating mode.

field.name: number_of_bunches
field.doc: MODULE accelerator-probe.

field.name: bunch_distance
field.doc: MODULE accelerator-probe. Time between bunches; it sets the step of a delay changed by bunch selection.

field.name: bunch_length
field.doc: MODULE accelerator-probe.

group.name: beam_pump
group.doc: The pump beam at the interaction point. It defines time zero.

field.name: associated_source
field.doc: Path to ``source_pump``. FROM NXmpes: not in the NXbeam base class.

field.name: incident_wavelength
field.doc: Central wavelength of the pump.

field.name: pulse_energy
field.doc: Pump energy per pulse at the interaction point: an array of length nE when it is measured per event.

field.name: pulse_duration
field.doc: Intensity full width at half maximum, as NXbeam defines it. A duration measured or simulated in another convention is converted before it is written here.

field.name: incident_polarization_stokes
field.doc: Stokes vector in the NeXus frame, as NXbeam defines it. A label such as p or s depends on the sample's plane of incidence and is not a substitute; write it in ``polarization_label`` as well if it is what the scientists use.

field.name: polarization_label
field.doc: PROPOSED. Polarization relative to the plane of incidence on the sample.

field.name: spot_size
field.doc: MODULE high-intensity. PROPOSED. Size of the focal spot along the two axes of the beam's reference frame. NXbeam/extent is a rectangular full width at half maximum and is not the same quantity as a Gaussian waist, so this field carries its definition.

field.name: peak_intensity
field.doc: MODULE high-intensity. PROPOSED. Peak intensity at focus, for example in W/cm^2. A derived value; the attribute says how it was derived.

field.name: normalized_vector_potential
field.doc: MODULE high-intensity. PROPOSED. Peak normalized vector potential a0, the quantity particle-in-cell inputs (PICMI) use for relativistic lasers. Derived; the attribute says how.

group.name: temporal_contrast
group.doc: MODULE high-intensity. PROPOSED. Intensity of the pulse's leading edge relative to its peak, as a function of time before the peak. A contrast is only meaningful with the time it refers to, so it is stored as a trace (or as single points with their times), never as one bare ratio.

field.name: time
field.doc: Time relative to the peak; negative before it.

field.name: method
field.doc: For example "third-order cross-correlation".

field.name: fluence
field.doc: MODULE surfaces. Fluence at the sample.

attribute.name: definition
attribute.doc: PROPOSED. Which area the energy is divided by: the beam's cross-section, or its footprint on the sample surface. They differ by the sine of the grazing angle and are often confused at grazing incidence.

field.name: depends_on
field.doc: MODULE surfaces. The pump's direction and incidence on the sample, through NXtransformations.

group.name: beam_probe
group.doc: The probe beam at the interaction point.

field.name: associated_source
field.doc: Path to ``source_probe``. FROM NXmpes, as for ``beam_pump``.

field.name: incident_energy
field.doc: Photon or particle energy of the probe. For an optical probe, ``incident_wavelength`` instead.

field.name: pulse_duration
field.doc: Together with the pump duration and the jitter, this bounds the time resolution.

field.name: extent
field.doc: Probe size at the sample, for checking that the pump covers the probed area.

field.name: focusing
field.doc: PROPOSED. Whether the probe is collimated, converging or diverging at the sample (an item of the HELPMI optical probe beam).

field.name: chirp_type
field.doc: Whether an optical probe is transform-limited or chirped at the sample (``NXbeam/chirp_type``; HELPMI asks for it).

field.name: pulse_delay
field.doc: Delay of the probe after the pump at the interaction point: positive when the probe arrives later. The best value available; when an arrival-time correction has been applied, the uncorrected readback is kept through ``@variant``. An array of length nE when it changes from event to event.

attribute.name: reference_beam
attribute.doc: PROPOSED. Path to the beam the delay is measured from: this entry's ``/ENTRY/INSTRUMENT/beam_pump``, e.g. ``/entry/instrument/beam_pump``. Not an enumeration, because a validator compares an enumeration with the literal value, and no file path is the template.

attribute.name: synchronization
attribute.doc: PROPOSED. Path to the NXsynchronization group that makes this delay valid.

field.name: pulse_delay_set
field.doc: The delay that was asked for. Differs from ``pulse_delay`` by the readback error and any correction.

group.name: synchronization
group.doc: What the delay is held against. PROPOSED base class; see NXsynchronization.nxdl.xml.

field.name: locked
field.doc: MODULE accelerator-probe.

field.name: reference_frequency
field.doc: MODULE accelerator-probe.

field.name: frequency_ratio
field.doc: MODULE accelerator-probe.

field.name: arrival_time_correction
field.doc: MODULE accelerator-probe.

group.doc: MODULE high-repetition. Readbacks on their own clock, for example the lock state or the PLL phase error over time.
Detectors. The technique's own definition says what they hold; this definition adds only timing and provenance.

field.name: trigger_delay_time_set
field.doc: MODULE accelerator-probe. The gate of a detector that selects one probe pulse per pump pulse.

group.name: technical_metadata
group.doc: MODULE provenance. The device as built: manufacturer, model, serial number, calibration and its date (HELPMI DDC category A).

group.name: procedural_metadata
group.doc: MODULE provenance. The device as used: location, exposure, gain, trigger, gate, filters, and the date of the last zero-delay image (HELPMI DDC category B).

group.name: security_metadata
group.doc: MODULE provenance. Access conditions: which of the device's metadata may be published (HELPMI DDC category C). Laser quality-assurance data are often kept internal.

field.name: identifier
field.doc: MODULE surfaces. PROPOSED. A persistent identifier for a sample that survives the measurement, for example an IGSN. A target destroyed by each shot (MODULE high-intensity) is described instead (``name``, ``description``) and its position per event recorded in an NXpositioner.

group.doc: MODULE high-intensity. The target position for each event, when each shot uses a fresh spot of the target.

group.name: simulation_links
group.doc: MODULE simulation. Links to simulations run for this entry, one NXnote per link, following HZDR's metadata.simulation link object: the openPMD series, the matched iteration, the code and its version. Simulation data are referenced, never copied.
